name: manual_5b40f2
claim: A batch script that switches branches, cherry-picks, or force-pushes against a shared canonical repo checkout must run in an isolated git worktree (git worktree add --detach <path> origin/main), never cd into the live directory other sessions/agents are actively using.

decisions.notes: ClineBot's /tmp/reanchor_all.sh cd'd into the live orama-system checkout and did 15 rounds of checkout -B/cherry-pick/force-push directly against it while a Claude Code session was concurrently committing there. Observed symptom: git rev-parse HEAD returned different values on consecutive calls, and a Windows .cmd file showed as spuriously modified — both resolved on their own once the concurrent process settled, but it could easily have collided destructively. Fixed by wrapping the whole script in a worktree (git worktree add --detach), confirmed via dry-run that the canonical checkout's branch pointer is untouched throughout. Two more bugs found and fixed in the same script: (1) 'mv .gitattributes .gitattributes.bak' followed immediately by 'git checkout -- .' silently restored the file, making the intended EOL-handling-disable a complete no-op every run — confirmed empirically in a scratch repo before fixing; reordered so the hide happens after the working-tree reset, not before. (2) The failure path called 'git rebase --abort' but the script only ever uses 'git cherry-pick' — dead command, replaced with the correct 'git cherry-pick --abort'.
